title: Quantifying Pauli Errors in Single-Photon Resource-State Generation
authors: Yuktee Gupta, Andrew C. Doherty, Sahand Mahmoodian
abstract: We propose a scheme to compute Pauli error rates in photonics-based quantum error correction using experimental observables of single photons produced from quantum emitters. We show that first-order coherence measurements and first-order cross correlations, which can be implemented using photon counting, can extract single-photon and entangled single-photon wavefunctions in the presence of imperfections due to photon distinguishability, laser noise, and photon loss. Leveraging this, we show that the wavefunction of any entangled state of noisy photons produced from a single quantum emitter can be expressed in matrix-product-state form and can be used to analytically compute the expectation value of the stabilizer generators of the corresponding entangled state. From this we obtain analytic expressions for the Pauli error probabilities in terms of the photon noise parameters. Furthermore, we calculate Pauli error maps for entangled photons after undergoing Bell- state measurements in terms of these parameters. Our work provides a method to use experimental measurements to determine the required quality of photons produced from quantum emitters for fault-tolerant fusion-based photonics quantum computing.
summary: This work presents a comprehensive method to characterize the fidelity of entangled single-photon resources emitted from quantum emitters. By measuring first-order coherence functions, researchers can reconstruct the full state and analytically derive Pauli error probabilities associated with subsequent fusion measurements. This provides crucial guidelines for improving photon sources for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
main_problem: The paper develops a method to compute Pauli error rates for entangled single-photon resource states generated from quantum emitters, bridging continuous field measurements with discrete qubit error models.
main_result: Analytic expressions for Pauli error probabilities are derived purely as functions of experimentally measurable parameters like first-order coherence function values and transmission coefficients.
method: The authors use first-order coherence measurements ($G^{(1)}$) to reconstruct the full quantum state ($\hat{ho}$) and then calculate stabilizer expectation values to determine the associated Pauli error maps for fusion operations.
model_or_system: The system involves single-photon sources based on multi-level quantum emitters (three- or four-level), which generate entangled states used in photonic quantum computing circuits.
key_observables: First-order coherence function $G^{(1)}(x_1, x_2)$, Pauli error probabilities ($p_x, p_y, p_z$), and stabilizer expectation values ($\langle\hat{O}angle$).
important_parameters: Photon noise parameters, transmission coefficient $\eta$, and coupling constants derived from emitter properties.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to measure $G^{(1)}$ to reconstruct the state; error calculations are performed up to first order in experimental parameters.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate level schemes for three-level and four-level emitters, pulse sequences for generating entangled states (GHZ/cluster), and dual-rail fusion circuit setups.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from characterizing the emitted state using $G^{(1)}$ measurements to modeling the error process via Pauli maps applied during a fusion operation on multi-photon resource states.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, experimentally measurable pathway (via coherence functions) to quantify fundamental noise sources that limit fault-tolerant quantum computation in photonic platforms.
